tests.description: Reference: the real64 (-fdefault-real-8) standalone kernels/cldfra_driver of the ctessum-claude/WRF fork, which calls cal_cldfra1 EXTRACTED VERBATIM from phys/module_radiation_driver.F at build time (kernels/Makefile rule cldfra_kernels.F90), so the reference cannot drift from the model code. Inputs are the dumped t3d, p3d, qv3d, qc3d, qi3d and qs3d of the column named below (single-precision values widened), narrowed to a one-column tile by tools/prep_cldfra_dumps.py. The scheme is a pure diagnostic (no time step), so no small-dt replay is involved and no dt sensitivity applies. Why the real64 replay and not the CLDFRA the model itself wrote: the Randall branch divides the condensate by (RHGRID QVS_WEIGHT - QV)^GAMMA, a cancellation of two near-equal numbers, and near saturation that costs WRF's single-precision arithmetic up to 5.1e-5 absolute -- 1.2e-4 relative -- which is far coarser than the rel 1e-5 contract for real32 references. Evaluating this component's own expressions in binary32 reproduces the in-model CLDFRA to 6.0e-8 absolute, so the gap is WRF's arithmetic and not the transcription. Against the real64 kernel the residual is binary64 roundoff (measured over all five regimes: <= 4.3e-16 absolute in cldfra), so the column tolerances are abs 1e-12 -- about 1e-12 of the field's unit range and roughly a thousand times the measured error -- and the spot checks rel 1e-9, the double-precision contract. The `branch` column is the Fortran's cldfra1_flag and is exact. Assertions: Linf_error of the whole cldfra and branch columns against the inline reference, plus spot checks of cldfra at every layer the scheme returns a strictly fractional value for. Regime: the first radiation call of the em_scm_xy reference run (call 1, 19:00 UTC start), column 1 of the tile -- a COMPLETELY CLOUD-FREE column, and the one regime that pins the condensate guard rather than the fit. Not one of the 59 layers holds QCLDMIN of condensate, so every layer takes branch 1 and cldfra is identically zero. That is not a trivial answer: the Murray over-water fit is extrapolated far outside its range at stratospheric temperatures, and layers 55-59 come out at RHUM between 1 and 27.4, so without the QCLD < QCLDMIN test those five layers would be handed back as fully cloudy. Mutation-checked: dropping the guard from `cldfra` leaves the other five regimes green and fails here.

A thin glaciated cloud at layers 51-57: seven layers hold condensate and every one of them is pure ice (the condensate weight (qi + qs)/QCLD is 1 to within 1e-3 everywhere), so the saturation is judged entirely against the over-ice Murray fit. All three arms fire -- 52 cloud-free layers (branch 1), three layers at or above RHGRID forced to exactly 1 (branch 2) and four on the Randall fit (branch 3), spanning 0.021 to 0.996.
